title: Schedule A (Itemized Deductions): required when the computed Schedule A total (line 8a Form 1098 home-mortgage interest, the only populated category for this bounded class) strictly exceeds the standard deduction (ADR-0036, Track 0 Sec 8). Deterministic tie favors the standard deduction, matching the tax.us.2025.rule.form1040-line12e max() semantics and the milestone's exclusion of voluntary itemization. Reuses the subtotal-over-threshold-parameter(default-zero) shape already proven by attachment.f8949.json / attachment.schedule-d.v3.json, expressing the dynamic standard-deduction comparison as the single tax.us.2025.schedule-a.excess-over-standard signed-difference subtotal so no new attachment ontology is required. Repair round 3 finding 2: bumped from attachment-rule.v1 to attachment-rule.v4 (ADR-0055 Decision 1) to admit value-checked completeness.required_answers (check: "value", equals: "yes") for the seven schedule-a-boundary -declared facts, so the whole attachment - and therefore the whole Schedule A computation - is required-and-incomplete unless every category's absence is genuinely declared "yes", not merely present with any value. The single itemization part is migrated to attachment-rule.v2+'s authority/row_sets shape (single_family authority over tax.us.2025.f1098, one row_set whose subtotal_symbol is tax.us.2025.schedule-a.line8a itself), reproducing the runner's own legacy rows/tie_out default (subtotal_symbol = tie_out.line_symbol) exactly - no behavior change, only the schema-required shape.
